name: Zephyr Bissap-Lime
description: A clean, high-acid sparkling soda combining bissap (dried hibiscus-adjacent variant with deeper tannin notes) with real lime juice, producing a very dark ruby soda with a sharp, wine-adjacent tartness. Positioned in the Tier 3 market as a sophisticated non-alcoholic option.
flavor_profile: Dark, tannic hibiscus-bissap with real lime acid sharpness, very dry finish, almost wine-like in its complexity; high carbonation that amplifies the tartness
cultural_context: Zephyr Bissap-Lime is the soda for people who want to signal that they have taste without spending Luma money. Its dark color, dry profile, and wine-adjacent complexity make it the non-alcoholic choice at Tier 3 social events where alcohol is present but not required. It has a secondary following among people who have given up alcohol but don't want to drink something that reads as soft. The slogan is intentionally a little aggressive.
story_hooks: Zephyr's 'real lime juice' sourcing comes from a greenhouse co-op in the city's northern reclaimed zone — the co-op is about to lose its land lease and has given Zephyr an ultimatum: buy the land or lose the supply contract.

A Tier 4 sommelier has started including Zephyr Bissap-Lime in blind tasting panels alongside natural wines — and it has outscored several bottles in the Φ80-100 range, which multiple corponations find commercially threatening.

Someone is using Zephyr's dark color and opaque bottle to conceal a look-alike product with a very different ingredient list — and the substitution is happening at the distribution level, not the retail level.
